title: Utilise and perform minor repair and maintenance tasks on implements, equipment and infrastructure

lessons.title: Selecting tools, implements and equipment
lessons.html:
Matching equipment to the job

Most farm processes use a combination of tools and implements. For example, establishing a vegetable land can involve a tractor with a ripper and disc harrow, a ridger, a knapsack sprayer for weeds, hand hoes, and irrigation equipment. Choosing the right combination makes the work faster, better and safer.

How to select

  1. Understand the task: what must be done, where, and to what standard. Ask your supervisor.
  2. Check conditions: soil type and moisture, slope, crop stage, weather.
  3. Choose suitable equipment from what the farm has, for example:
    • Fencing: wire strainer, fencing pliers, droppers, post-hole digger, crowbar.
    • Weed control: hoe, slasher, brush cutter (trained users), knapsack sprayer (trained users).
    • Feeding livestock: wheelbarrow, feed scoop, troughs, bakkie or trailer.
    • Irrigation repairs: pipe cutter, joiners, spanners, spade.
  4. Check that it works before taking it to the field.
  5. Collect PPE for the job.

Example: repairing a camp fence

A storm has knocked down a section of fence in a cattle camp. The team takes a bakkie with a trailer, a post-hole digger and crowbar for new posts, a wire strainer and fencing pliers, a roll of wire, droppers, and gloves and safety glasses for everyone. They check the strainer works and the pliers cut cleanly before leaving the yard, so the job is finished in one trip and the cattle cannot get out onto the road.

Using implements correctly

  • Follow the operator's manual and your training.
  • Only trained and authorised people hitch implements to tractors and operate them.
  • Check implement settings, such as depth on a ripper or nozzle type on a sprayer, with your supervisor.
  • Use equipment within its limits. An overloaded trailer or a slasher used on thick bush will break.

lessons.title: Monitoring condition and minor repairs
lessons.html:
Daily checks

Check equipment before, during and after use. Look, listen and feel:

  • Loose, missing or broken bolts, pins and clips.
  • Worn or damaged blades, tines, discs and nozzles.
  • Cracks in frames and welds.
  • Leaks of oil, fuel or water.
  • Flat or damaged tyres.
  • Missing guards and shields.
  • Unusual noises or vibration.
  • Grease points dry.

Minor repairs you may do

Do only repairs you are trained for and allowed to do. Examples:

ItemMinor repair
Hand toolsReplace handles, tighten heads, sharpen
WheelbarrowRepair or replace tube, tighten bolts
Knapsack sprayerReplace nozzles, washers and seals (after cleaning)
ImplementsReplace shear bolts, worn tines or points, lynch pins; tighten bolts
Fences and gatesRe-strain wire, replace droppers, oil hinges
IrrigationReplace drippers, join cut pipes
TroughsReplace float valves, clean

Repair safely

  • Switch off machines, remove the key and wait for parts to stop.
  • Lower implements to the ground or support them on stands before working under them. Never rely on hydraulics alone.
  • Clean chemical equipment before repairing it and wear gloves.
  • Use the right spare parts. A normal bolt in place of a shear bolt can wreck the implement.
  • Use correct tools: the right size spanner, not pliers on nuts.
  • Test the repair before use.

When to stop using equipment

Stop at once and report if a guard is missing, brakes or lights on a trailer do not work, a frame is cracked, or something makes a new noise. Tag the item "Do not use" so nobody else takes it out by mistake.

Report bigger problems, such as cracked frames, gearbox noise or hydraulic leaks, to the workshop.

lessons.title: Maintenance, storage and safety
lessons.html:
Routine maintenance

  • Clean equipment after use: remove soil, plant material and manure. Wash sprayers out thoroughly as instructed, away from water sources.
  • Lubricate: grease all grease nipples on the schedule; oil chains and moving parts.
  • Tighten bolts and check pins and clips.
  • Sharpen or replace worn cutting parts.
  • Check tyre pressures on trailers and implements.
  • Protect from rust: paint scratched areas or oil bare metal on tillage tools before storage.
  • Keep records of maintenance and repairs, with the date and what was done.

Storing equipment to specification

  • Store implements under cover, on level ground, lowered or on stands, so they cannot fall.
  • Release spring tension and hydraulic pressure where the manual says.
  • Keep the store tidy with clear walkways.
  • Hang hand tools on racks; keep sharp edges covered.
  • Store fuel, oil and chemicals in their own stores, not with equipment.
  • Drain water from pumps and sprayers in frost areas.
  • Lock away valuable equipment to prevent theft.

Safety measures

  • Wear PPE: safety boots, gloves, overalls, safety glasses when grinding, cutting or hammering, hearing protection near loud machines.
  • Never step over a turning PTO shaft. Keep all guards in place.
  • Never ride on implements or drawbars.
  • Stand clear when tractors hitch or unhitch implements.
  • Lift heavy parts with help or lifting equipment.
  • Keep fire extinguishers and first aid kits in the workshop.
  • The OHS Act 85 of 1993 requires safe machinery and safe work methods; report unsafe equipment.

Key points

  • Select the right combination of tools and implements for the task and conditions.
  • Check equipment before, during and after use.
  • Do only minor repairs you are trained for, with machines off and supported.
  • Use correct spare parts, especially shear bolts.
  • Clean, grease and store equipment under cover, lowered and safe.

quiz.question: What should you do first when selecting equipment for a task?

options.text: Understand the task and the standard required

quiz.question: Why must a shear bolt be replaced with the correct shear bolt?

options.text: A normal bolt can let the implement be wrecked

quiz.question: Before working under an implement, what must you do?

options.text: Lower it or support it on stands
Raise it as high as possible

quiz.question: Which is a minor repair a trained worker may do?

options.text: Replacing nozzles on a knapsack sprayer
Welding a cracked frame without training
Under cover, on level ground, lowered or on stands

quiz.question: It is safe to step over a turning PTO shaft if you are quick.
